# Length-based indicators

Length-based indicators (LBIs) summarise each length composition in a few
numbers that can be compared with reference levels or followed over time. The
empirical indicators need no model fit and only Linf and L50 (for some, also
M/k), so they can be computed at the start of an assessment and by analysts
without modelling experience. The model-based indicators (`LBIspr`, `LBImean`)
use the fitted selectivity and growth.

## Empirical indicators (no model)

`lbi_flicc()` computes, for each gear and year, the indicators of ICES WKLIFE
and of Froese (2004), the reference lengths, and a Beverton-Holt estimate of
total mortality from the mean length:

| Indicator | Definition | Reference (green) | Limit (red below) | Property |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lc/L50, L25/L50 | length at half the modal abundance; 25th percentile | 1 | 0.75 | conservation of immatures |
| Lmax5/Linf, L95/Linf | mean of the largest 5%; 95th percentile | 0.8 | 0.7 | conservation of large fish |
| Pmega | proportion above 1.1 Lopt | 0.3 | 0.15 | conservation of large fish |
| LmaxY/Lopt, Lmean/Lopt | class of maximum catch biomass; mean length above Lc | 0.9 | 0.75 | optimal yield |
| Lmean/LFM | LFM = 0.75 Lc + 0.25 Linf, the mean length at F = M | 1 | 0.9 | MSY proxy |
| Pobj (Cope-Punt) | Pmat + Popt + Pmega, with a decision tree | see below | – | spawning biomass vs 0.4 B0 |

The traffic light has three colours: green at or above the ICES reference level,
orange between the limit and the reference level, red below the limit. The
limits are pragmatic choices (10-25% below the reference level, half of it for
Pmega) that separate a clear departure from a marginal one; they can be changed
with `limits`, e.g. `limits = c("Lmean/LFM" = 0.85)`.

with $L_{opt} = 2/3\,L_\infty$ (or $L_\infty\,3/(3 + M/k)$ with `Lopt = "mk"`),
and the proportions of mature fish (`Pmat`), of fish around Lopt (`Popt`) and
their sum `Pobj`. Cope and Punt (2009) use `Pobj` to identify the selectivity
pattern of the fishery (below 1: mainly small and immature fish; between 1 and 2:
selection close to the maturity ogive; 2: only mature fish of optimal size and
larger), and then `Pmat` or `Popt` to judge whether spawning biomass is at or above
the target of 0.4 B0 (`cp_selectivity`, `cp_test`, `cp_status`). A fishery that
takes only fish of optimal size gives no information on status. `catch_by_gear` adds the gears pooled into
one composition raised by catch (`combine_lfd()`), as gear `"pooled"`:

```{r lbi-empirical, fig.height = 8}
lbi <- lbi_flicc(lfd, lhpar, catch_by_gear = c(Trawl = 0.95, Gillnet = 0.05))
lbi$values[lbi$values$year == 2024, c("gear", "Lc", "Lmean", "LFM", "L95", "Lmax5", "Pmat", "Pmega", "Z")]
lbi$values[lbi$values$year == 2024, c("gear", "Pobj", "cp_selectivity", "cp_test", "cp_status")]
plot_lbi(lbi)
```

```{r lbi-trend, fig.height = 6}
plot_lbi(lbi, type = "trend")
```

How to read them:

- The trawl catches mainly immature fish (Lc/L50 about 0.6), so the indicators
  for immatures and large fish are below their reference levels in every year;
  for this gear they describe its selectivity as much as the stock. The gillnet
  catches the larger fish and meets most reference levels. Indicators are
  therefore read **by gear**, and against each gear's own history.
- By the Cope-Punt tree, the gillnet selects close to the maturity ogive, and
  the proportion mature is mostly below the threshold for SB at or above 0.4 B0;
  the trawl takes mainly small fish with too few mature fish. Both point to SB
  below the target, in line with the SPR of the model (about 0.2).
  The tree has a threshold at Pobj = 1: in 2013-2014 the gillnet's Pobj is just
  below 1, the weaker test on Pmat then applies, and the status switches to
  "SB >= target". Near the branch points, read the tree's result with caution.
- The indicators of the upper tail (Lmax5, L95, Pmega) identify overfishing
  best; those of the left limb (Lc, L25) also respond to recruitment (Kell et al.
  2022).
- Indicators follow **trends** better than they classify status: the reference
  levels depend on Linf, L50 and M/k. Where a period is known when the stock was
  in a good state, indicators relative to that period avoid this dependence
  (Kell and Sharma 2025):

```{r lbi-relative, fig.height = 6}
lbi_ref <- lbi_flicc(lfd, lhpar, ref_years = 2013:2015)
plot_lbi(lbi_ref, type = "relative")
```

Here the large-fish indicators and the proportion mature have increased since
2013-2015 and the mean-length estimate of Z has decreased: the size structure has
improved over the period, in line with the decrease in F estimated by the model.

## LBIspr

For each gear, `LBIspr()` compares the observed proportion of large fish with
the proportion expected at the reference $F_{\mathrm{SPR}x}$:

1. Equilibrium numbers-at-length at $F_{\mathrm{SPR}x}$, $N^{ref}(L)$, and the
   reference catch composition of gear $g$, $v_g(L) = N^{ref}(L) S_g(L)$ (retained
   bins only, i.e. below the tail cut).
2. Threshold length $L^*_g$: the length at which the cumulative $v_g$ reaches the
   fraction `thresh` (default 0.75) of its total.
3. Reference proportion above the threshold,
   $P^{ref}_g = \sum_{L \ge L^*_g} v_g(L) / \sum_L v_g(L)$ (about $1 -$ `thresh`).
4. Observed proportion in year $y$,
   $P^{obs}_{g,y} = \sum_{L \ge L^*_g} y_{g,y,L} / \sum_L y_{g,y,L}$.
5. Indicator $\mathrm{LBI}_{g,y} = P^{obs}_{g,y}/P^{ref}_g$.

$\mathrm{LBI} = 1$: as many large fish as at the target; $< 1$: fewer, i.e. F above
$F_{\mathrm{SPR}x}$. The threshold lengths are returned as `attr(, "Lref")`.

```{r lbispr}
lbi <- LBIspr(fit, spr = 40, thresh = 0.75)
attr(lbi, "Lref")
plot_LBIspr(fit, thresh = 0.75)
plot_LBIp(fit, year = 2024)
```

## LBImean

`LBImean()` is the model-based analogue of the ICES mean-length indicator
$\bar L/L_{F=M}$: the reference mean length (above `lc`, default the gear's
50% selectivity length) is computed from the fitted model at $F = M$
(`ref = "FM"`) or at $F_{\mathrm{SPR}x}$ (`ref = "spr"`), using the fitted growth
variability and gear selectivity, including domes.

```{r lbimean}
LBImean(fit, ref = "FM")
```

## Indicators and the tail cut

Both indicators use the fit's tail cut by default (`tail_cut = NULL`), so the
indicator and the likelihood use the same bins; `tail_cut = FALSE` uses all bins.

## Check 10: indicators against status

| | |
|---|---|
| **Look for** | LBIspr and SPR/SPR40 telling the same story; similar indicators across gears. |
| **Red flags** | Gears disagreeing strongly (selectivity misfit or sampling); indicator noise much larger than the SPR trend. |
| **Action** | Use the more informative gear; pool gears (`pool` in `flicc.sa()`); smooth in the harvest control rule. |
